resources.string: International Space Station\nLabel, orbit and ground track
Space stations\nTiangong, visiting craft and other crewed vehicles
Recent launches\nObjects launched in the last 30 days
Navigation (GNSS)\nGPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou, about 20,000 km up
SatNOGS\nAbout 600 tracked by the SatNOGS ground station network
Geostationary\nAbout 570 active, 35,786 km up. Pinch out to see the belt; tap one for details
GEO protected zone\nThe inactive satellites and debris around the geostationary belt, about 300
Highly elliptical orbits\nAbout 40, e.g. Molniya-type and science missions out to 170,000 km. Pinch far out to see them
Medium Earth orbit\nOther active satellites between 2,000 and 35,000 km
OneWeb\nEutelsat OneWeb broadband: about 650, 1,200 km up
Amazon Leo\nAmazon broadband (Project Kuiper): about 390 so far
Guowang\nChina\'s national broadband network (SatNet) and its test satellites: about 200
Orbcomm\nMachine-to-machine messaging and ship tracking: about 15
Planet\nEarth imaging (Dove, SkySat and Pelican): about 100
Spire\nWeather, ship and aircraft tracking (Lemur): about 90
Other low Earth orbit\nAll other active satellites under 2,000 km: about 2,700
Debris\nAbout 2,700 pieces from the 2007 Fengyun-1C ASAT test and the 2009 Iridium 33 / Cosmos 2251 collision
Day and night\nShade the night side, and dim satellites in Earth\'s shadow
Visible ISS passes\nA notification 5 minutes before the ISS crosses your sky while you can see it. Set for the next 3 days each time the app opens
Notifications are turned off for WhatsUp, so pass alerts can\'t be shown.
When a satellite is about to cross your sky
Look %1$s; it climbs to %2$d° and fades in the %3$s
Orbit paths\nEach satellite\'s orbit, drawn at altitude
Ground tracks\nWhere the orbit passes over the surface
Altitude lines\nFrom each satellite straight down to the ground
My location\nYour position and its accuracy circle
Location permission denied — the globe can\'t centre on you.
Using the phone\'s GPS and network location
Couldn\'t find \"%1$s\". Try latitude and longitude (53.55, -113.5 or 53°33\'N 113°30\'W), MGRS (12U VD 41533 41226), or a fuller address. Addresses need a connection.

Orbital data, satellite catalogue and close approaches (SOCRATES): CelesTrak. Launches: The Space Devs\' Launch Library 2. Stars: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, via d3-celestial. Positions worked out on this phone with SGP4 (satellite.js). Globe: MapLibre. Map tiles: as credited on the map.
Coverage footprints\nWhere on the ground the selected satellite is above the horizon (and 10° up)
Orbital planes\nThe rings the big constellations fly in: Starlink, OneWeb, GNSS and others shown
Launches\nUpcoming launches at their launch pads, from Launch Library
Stars, Sun and Moon\nThe real night sky behind the globe and in sky view; the Sun and Moon (tap them for rise, set and phases)
True-scale Sun and Moon\nDraw them at their real size, however small, on the globe and in sky view. Sky view always does over the camera
Starred satellites\' passes\nA notification 5 minutes before each pass over 10° of a satellite you\'ve starred (★ in its info)
Rises in the %1$s, climbs to %2$d°, sets in the %3$s
